content: Your doctor has prescribed sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim, a combination antibiotic, to treat your infection. This medication will be administered intravenously, mixed with a fluid that will drip through a needle or catheter placed in your vein. The infusion typically lasts 60 to 90 minutes or longer and is given two to four times daily. The combination of sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim works by eliminating bacteria responsible for various infections, including pneumonia, urinary tract infections, and intestinal infections. In some cases, this medication may be used for other purposes; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Your healthcare provider will monitor the effectiveness of your treatment and any potential side effects through laboratory tests and physical examinations. It is crucial to attend all scheduled appointments with your doctor and the laboratory. The duration of your treatment will depend on how your infection and symptoms respond to the medication. Precautions Before Administration: Inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to sulfamethoxazole, trimethoprim, other sulfa drugs, diuretics (water pills), oral diabetes medications, or any other drugs. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially anticoagulants (blood thinners) like warfarin (Coumadin), cyclosporine (Neoral, Sandimmune), diabetes medications, diuretics, seizure medications like phenytoin (Dilantin), methotrexate (Folex, Rheumatrex), and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have a history of alcoholism or if you currently have or have had liver or kidney disease, asthma, severe allergies, anemia, or glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G-6-PD) deficiency, an inherited blood disorder. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking this medication, contact your doctor immediately. Administering Your Medication: Before administering sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim, inspect the solution carefully. It should be clear and free of any floating particles. Gently squeeze the bag or check the container to ensure there are no leaks. Do not use the solution if it is discolored, contains particles, or if the bag or container is leaking. Replace it with a new solution and show the damaged one to your healthcare provider. It is essential to follow your healthcare provider's instructions precisely when using this medication. Do not stop your treatment prematurely, as this could worsen your infection and potentially lead to hospitalization. Do not alter your dosing schedule without consulting your healthcare provider. If you experience a mechanical issue, such as a blockage in the tubing, needle, or catheter, stop the infusion and contact your healthcare provider immediately to ensure your therapy continues without interruption. Side Effects: Minor Side Effects: Sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim may cause minor side effects. Notify your healthcare provider if any of the following symptoms are severe or persistent: Dizziness or loss of balance Loss of appetite Upset stomach Severe Side Effects: If you experience any of the following symptoms, contact your healthcare provider immediately: Sore throat Difficulty breathing Fever Headache Joint or muscle aches Yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice) Swelling of the lips or tongue Difficulty swallowing Skin rash or changes in the skin Fatigue Unusual bleeding or bruising Weakness Paleness Cough Diarrhea If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may report it to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Storing Your Medication: Your healthcare provider will likely instruct you on how to prepare each dose of sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim. Since the medication remains stable for only a short time after preparation, prepare your daily doses as directed. Store the medication as instructed by your healthcare provider. Ensure you understand the proper storage requirements for your medication. Keep your supplies in a clean, dry place when not in use, and store all medications and supplies out of reach of children. Your healthcare provider will also explain how to safely dispose of used needles, syringes, tubing, and containers to prevent accidental injury. In Case of Emergency or Overdose: If an overdose occurs, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Signs of Infection: If you are receiving sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim intravenously or subcutaneously, be aware of the symptoms of a catheter-related infection, which occurs at the site where the needle enters your vein or skin.
